sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a commencement rule only the draft states, applied to the publication date only the final documents give, then measured against the grace period's end; medium. Quick test survived (user chat 2026-10-13); no difficulty result yet.
- Dependency plan: D08 L37 or D04 L92 (3 months following publication) -> D05 L13 or D06 L12 with L106 (published 26 June 2024) -> 26 September 2024 (c1) -> D05 L110 or D06 L1171 (grace period ends 1 January 2025) -> 97 days (c2).
- Universe: not applicable (one derived date and one derived count).
- Necessity: the 3-month clause is printed only in D08 L37 and restated only in D04 L92 (searched all fourteen documents for "3 months", "three months", "following publication", "following the publication": no hit in D01, D02, D05 or D06; D06 L1174 says only that the dates "reflect consideration of feedback"). Without both, the first answer cannot be formed. The publication date and the grace period's end are only in D05 and D06 (searched "26 June", "June 2024", "1 January 2025", "grace period": D01 and D08 stop at 18 December 2023). Without both, neither answer can be formed. Each group is ticked with its alternative.
- Selected-lever checks: edition: the rule is the draft's (18 December 2023), the dates are the final documents' (26 June 2024). Calculation: both answers are derived; neither is printed anywhere.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Wrong year or edition: three months from the draft's own cover date (D08 L9 "Date of publication: 18 December 2023") gives 18 March 2024, and 18 March 2024 to 1 January 2025 is 289 days. (2) Look-alike measure: three months from the in-force date (D05 L20, 1 July 2024) gives 1 October 2024 and 92 days. Considered and not declared: giving the actual date, 1 July 2024 and 184 days (the wording asks for the date under the draft clause); a 90-day reading of "3 months", 24 September 2024 and 99 days (the clause says months); inclusive counting, 98 (the question asks how many days before the end date the earlier date is, a plain difference).
- Calculation verification: script, 2026-10-13: date(2024, 6, 26) plus three calendar months = 26 September 2024; date(2025, 1, 1) - date(2024, 9, 26) = 97 days. Second route by months: 4 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 1 = 97. Convention: elapsed days, 26 September not counted, 1 January counted. Wrong routes by the same script: 92, 289, 184.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the bundle overview lists "3 months following publication for commencement" under Doc 12, "3 months proposed transition period" under Doc 11 and the dates 26 June 2024, 1 July 2024 and 1 January 2025 under Docs 3 and 14; it prints neither 26 September 2024 nor 97. No document prints either (searched "September 2024", "26 September", "97 days"). Shortest complete route is the ten steps above.
- Precision/readings: "the publication of the Amended Code" is the publication of the amending Code once made, 26 June 2024 (D05 L13; D05 L55-59 lists the "Commission 111 Contact Code (Amendment Version 2024)" at that date); the draft's own 18 December 2023 date is the draft's publication, and amendments could not come into force before the Code was made. "ended" is the date both final documents print for the end of the grace period. Open point for the form's "One defensible answer" check: whether a solver is allowed the 18 March 2024 reading.
- Completeness: all fourteen documents read; no capture gap. One NZ's missing page 3 is not used.
- Style/set review: q01 (dropped) used a different hook and documents; no shared answer path. i21 and i22 share the date-count lever and are not live.

sections.question: Under the draft amended 111 Contact Code's own commencement clause, on what date would the amendments have come into force, and how many days before the grace period ended is that?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 12, commencement clause of the draft amending instrument; Doc 11 restates it): the draft says the Amended Code comes into force on a date that is 3 months following the publication of the Amended Code.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 14, cover and status note; Doc 3 carries the same date): the amended Code was published on 26 June 2024. Its amendments in fact came into force on 1 July 2024, which is a different date from the publication date.
Step 3. Application (Doc 12 and Doc 14): the clause counts from publication, and 3 months after 26 June 2024 is 26 September 2024. That is the first answer.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 14, grace period clause; Doc 3 gives the same date): the grace period for complying with the amendments ends on 1 January 2025.
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 12 and Doc 14): September has 30 days, so the days left in it after the 26th number: 30 - 26 = 4
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 12 and Doc 14): October is one day longer than September, so its length in days is: 30 + 1 = 31
Step 7. Calculation (Doc 12 and Doc 14): October and November together hold: 31 + 30 = 61
Step 8. Calculation (Doc 12 and Doc 14): adding December, which is as long as October: 61 + 31 = 92
Step 9. Calculation (Doc 12 and Doc 14): with the days left in September: 92 + 4 = 96
Step 10. Final answer (Doc 12 and Doc 14): the first answer is the date from Step 3, 26 September 2024. Counting 1 January 2025 itself, the days from that date to the end of the grace period, the second answer, number: 96 + 1 = 97
